1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.

2.  The present petition has been filed under Section 482 Cr.PC seeking quashing of the FIR No.0073/2019 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC registered at PS Tigri, Delhi and the proceedings pursuant thereto, on the ground that the parties have arrived at a settlement.
3. Issue notice.
Learned APP for the State accepts notice.
4. Learned APP submits that since the present FIR has arisen out of the matrimonial dispute and the parties have amicably settled all their disputes, This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 09:15:42 the State has no objection in case the present FIR is quashed.

5. The petitioner no.1 (former husband), petitioner no.2 (father of the petitioner no.1) and the petitioner no.3 (sister of the petitioner no.1) as well as the respondent no.2 (former wife) are present in the Court.

They have been identified by their respective counsels and the Investigating Officer,
ASI Rajesh Kumar, PS Tigri, Delhi.
6. The brief facts of the case are that marriage between the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 was solemnised on 27.11.2017 at New Delhi according to Hindu rites and ceremonies.

sentences.text: On account of temperamental issues, certain disputes arose between the parties which led to litigation between them, including the registration of the present FIR.
8. The petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2, who are present today in the Court state that the disputes between them have been amicably resolved.

9. The learned counsel for the petitioner invites attention of the Court to the judgment dated 23.11.2021 passed in HMA No.24/2021 under Section 13B(2) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 wherein the terms of settlement, which was arrived at between petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2,
have been recorded.
10.
In terms of the said settlement, the petitioner no.1 has to pay total amount of 1.5 lakhs to the respondent no.2 towards all her claims of maintenance, permanent alimony etc.
Out of the said amount, an amount of 1 lakh has already been paid, the receipt of which is acknowledged by the respondent no.2.

The balance amount of 50,000/- has been paid today in the Court to the respondent no.2 by way of Manager's Cheque no.005736 dated 02.05.2023 drawn on HDFC Bank,
Kaushambi, Ghaziabad.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 09:15:42 11.

On a query made by the Court, the respondent no.2 has categorically stated that she has entered into a compromise with the petitioner no.1 out of her own will, without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is confirmed by the respondent no.2 that she has received the entire amount in terms of the settlement and she has no objection in case the FIR is quashed.
12.

In view of the fact that the parties have amicably settled their differences out of their own free will, volition and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would, therefore, be in the interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings emanating there from.
13. There is also no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.
Accordingly, FIR No.0073/2019 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC registered at PS Tigri, Delhi and proceedings emanating there from are hereby quashed.
14. The petition is disposed of.
15. Order be uploaded on the website of this Court.
VIKAS MAHAJAN, J MAY 16, 2023 MK
This is a digitally signed order.
